evidence.experimental_conditions: Betamethasone-17-valerate 0.12% in petrolatum; patch tested on 257 consecutive patients with allergic contact dermatitis.
evidence.support_text: Betamethasone-17-valerate (0.12% in petrolatum) caused positive patch test reactions in 5 out of 257 patients with allergic contact dermatitis. Clinical relevance was found in 3 cases.

evidence.support_text: In a recent study (PAULSEN et al., 1993) patch tests were performed with carvone 5% in petrolatum according to the standard procedure for patch testing and reading. evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with 10% isopropyl myristate in petrolatum, 4554 patients, tested between January 1992 and December 2001
evidence.support_text: Uter et al performed a retroactive study of dermatitis patients patch tested for sensitization to isopropyl myristate. Isopropyl myristate was tested in 20% petrolatum using 8117 patients and 10% petrolatum using 4554 patients between January 1992 and December 2001. The lower concentration had 9 doubtful reactions, 2 irritant reactions, 7 + reactions, and 1 ++/+++ reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with 20% isopropyl myristate in petrolatum, 8117 patients, tested between January 1992 and December 2001
evidence.support_text: Uter et al performed a retroactive study of dermatitis patients patch tested for sensitization to isopropyl myristate. Isopropyl myristate was tested in 20% petrolatum using 8117 patients and 10% petrolatum using 4554 patients between January 1992 and December 2001. The higher concentration had 43 doubtful reactions, 5 irritant reactions, 6 + reactions, and 2 ++/+++ reactions. The authors concluded that isopropyl myristate does not need to be tested for during routine patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 mM Lina-OOHs, 250 mM DEPMPO in reconstructed human epidermis (RHE), monitored by EPR
evidence.support_text: Figure 2 legend: EPR experimental spectrum of Lina-OOHs (10 mM)/DEPMPO (250 mM) in reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) together with computer simulation afforded spectra of spin-adducts DEPMPO-OH, DEPMPO-R and DEPMPO-OR, indicating formation of radical species. Control experiments with single Lina-OOHs or single DEPMPO did not give any signal.

evidence.assay_type: EPR spin-trapping in reconstructed human epidermis
evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of Lina-OOHs in acetone (10 mM) to reconstructed human epidermis pre-loaded with DEPMPO in HEPES (15 min, 37°C, 5% CO2). EPR spectroscopy detection.
evidence.support_text: Reconstructed human epidermis loaded with DEPMPO and then topically exposed to Lina-OOHs at 10 mM in acetone showed DEPMPO spin-adducts characteristic of carbon-centered, hydroxyl, and alkoxyl radicals. No signal was obtained with the spin-trap alone or with Lina-OOHs alone in RHE.
